machine: Windows amd64, Intel Core i7-9750H, loaded development host

actual_desktop_phase.reason: Automatic approval review rejected Chrome activation because it could not determine the current browser URL. The parent prohibited actual ScreenRegion capture afterward to avoid bypassing that review.

initial_synthetic_scroll_attempt.interpretation: The sampled-pixel matcher was active when the bound expired. Host compilation/startup also stalled during this period, so this timeout is not an isolated CPU benchmark. A separate baseline benchmark build was stopped without reporting timing results. A later soak dispatch was also stopped for a quiet API-trace window and produced no result.

paired_matcher_benchmark.fixture: Same deterministic sparse-text 720x600 RGBA viewport pair, shifted down 13 physical pixels, with the original generic scoring path retained as the reference
paired_matcher_benchmark.interpretation: About 71% less matcher time in this short paired benchmark. Sample positions, RGB distances, blank-row treatment, trimming and direction selection are unchanged. Regression tests require exact equality against the reference, including subimages, nonzero origins and alpha. This does not establish end-to-end screenshot latency.

verified: Exact final PNG pixels and periodic preview pixels
Stored strips retain every output pixel once
Native source work stops at the production 128-frame cap
Finished sessions release their strips and output buffers
Live Go heap stays near 10.13 MB at the last two checkpoints
synthetic_scroll_soak.limitations: Synthetic source only; no browser was scrolled. The timing includes matching, thumbnail generation and preview PNG encoding but excludes native capture and frontend decoding. The loaded-host p95/max tail remains significant, so actual scrolling smoothness is not claimed. Reserved Go heap rose to about 66.9 MB; that is distinct from live heap and from the app's full process tree.

encoding_cancellation_soak.scope: Real context cancellation after raster encoding has started on a generated 1920x1080 image; this is component cancellation latency, not hotkey-to-visible UI latency.

cancellation_regressions: Cancel propagates to the manual session context
Candidate search checks that context at most every 16 candidates
Canceled matching neither appends strips nor moves the observed frame/top
Long screenshot PNG export observes the same session context
